cells.tense: You are holding what came out of the first spark, and you know its weight exactly.
cells.ask: Tell someone just starting one specific thing you'd want said to you if you were starting now. Say it to them today.
cells.core:
You know what this took, and you're not pretending it was easy or that it was luck. You can see the weight of it, name it, and still hold the door open for whatever wants to come next.

You're tending it, not gripping it. What you made is real, and you can set it down on a table and keep an eye on it without hovering over it. That's hard after something took everything — but you're doing it, and what's around you can feel it. What you're free to put that toward next: the repayment you don't need, or the thing that hasn't asked for your help yet. Both are quiet. One is rest. One is the next seed.
cells.sheetLine: You carried it to the end and can keep it there without gripping it
cells.verb: carrying what the spark became, all the way to its end

cells.tense: You are already standing in what this will need to become, and you are bracing for it.
cells.ask: Before you add one more thing to what you're growing, look at what's actually there today and name just that.
cells.core:
You keep running ahead of what you made. It's finished, or close enough, and already you're rehearsing the next version, the next stage, the next thing it owes you.

Going well here looks like standing in the room with the thing as it is — half-grown or done, not three rooms ahead of it. What's bending it now is that you're bracing. You're spending the present on a version of this that hasn't arrived. What you finished put something real into the world. You can stand in front of it. What's growing right now is enough as it is.
cells.sheetLine: You're bracing for a stage that hasn't arrived yet
cells.verb: carrying what the spark became, all the way to its end

cells.tense: A door closed behind you, and you are still standing at it.
cells.ask: Show one thing you've already made — a photo, a page, whatever it is — to one person, and let them see it without calling it anything.
cells.core:
There's something you finished, and you don't point at it. That's why advice is hard to give: hard to stand behind something you'd rather not look at. So the finished thing sits there in the room, unlit, and you keep your hand off it.

Here's the small opening. Someone telling you what something is for, when you've already made it, gets you a stranger's picture of your own work. Someone showing you what they see gets you one more angle on something that already exists. The difference is small and it matters. The thing is not asking for a coach. It wants attention, and it will take the attention and hand back its own sense of what it is.
cells.sheetLine: You stopped pointing at what you made, and it's still there

cells.tense: You are already tending what's growing here, and you're filing it under just what anyone would do.
cells.ask: Name one thing you did today only because it was needed, and say out loud that you were the one who did it.
cells.core:
You've been growing something — a person, a habit, a piece of work — and the growing is yours. The timing was yours, the patience was yours, the steady hand was yours too. It gets called 'how I am' or 'just being there,' and that version leaves out the part that did the work.

It isn't a mood. It's a set of decisions, made mostly at small forks where the easier move was to not show up, and you've been making the other call. Saying so isn't taking credit. It's the difference between doing it again on purpose and doing it again by accident.
cells.sheetLine: The growing you've been doing is yours, not the situation's
cells.verb: carrying what the spark became, all the way to its end
